datasets.name: Disentangling the origins of confidence in speeded perceptual judgments through multimodal imaging
datasets.description: Simultaneous EEG and fMRI recordings from healthy volunteers who reported their confidence in the accuracy of decisions they either committed themselves or merely observed. The dataset supports analysis of postdecisional contributions to metacognition and includes raw fMRI, BrainVision EEG, T1 anatomical scans and field maps, along with preprocessed EEG and fMRI derivatives.
datasets.authors: Michael Pereira, Nathan Faivre, Inaki Iturrate, Marco Wirthlin, Luana Serafini, Stephanie Martin, Arnaud Desvachez, Olaf Blanke, Dimitri Van de Ville, Jose del R. Millan

datasets.name: Single-pulse open-loop TMS-EEG dataset
datasets.description: A single-pulse, open-loop transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) dataset with simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) recordings. The dataset is organized in BIDS format and mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro (ds002094).

datasets.name: Real-time EEG feedback on alpha power lateralization leads to behavioral improvements in a covert attention task
datasets.description: EEG recordings from fourteen healthy participants performing a covert spatial attention task across three sessions. The study tested real-time feedback of alpha power lateralization (α-LI) versus sham feedback in a single-blinded crossover design. It examined whether such neurofeedback leads to behavioral improvements in attention.
datasets.authors: Christoph Schneider, Michael Pereira, Luca Tonin, Jose del R. Millan

datasets.name: Rivalry_Tagging
datasets.description: Rivalry_Tagging is a neuroimaging dataset of binocular rivalry recordings collected between February and March 2014. Trials include events for pattern presentation (pattern1, pattern2), left and right tap responses, baseline periods, and non-rivalry color (green/red) conditions. Trigger channels (UDIO001, UPPT001) are provided to align stimulus and response events.
datasets.authors: Janine Mendola, Elizabeth Bock

datasets.name: PsiConnect
datasets.description: PsiConnect is a multimodal neuroimaging dataset examining context-dependent neural and subjective effects of psilocybin in 62 participants scanned before and after a 19 mg dose. It combines multi-echo functional, structural and diffusion-weighted MRI with EEG during resting state and three naturalistic conditions (guided meditation, music listening, movie watching). Half of the cohort completed an 8-week meditation training program. Behavioural and self-report measures with follow-ups up to one year support study of acute and longitudinal effects.
datasets.authors: Adeel Razi

datasets.name: Audiocue walking study
datasets.description: A mobile brain/body imaging (MoBI) dataset of 18 participants walking on a treadmill at constant speed while stepping in time to an auditory tone sequence. Participants adapted step length and rate to occasional shifts in the tempo of the pacing stimulus, to a faster or slower tempo. The dataset supports study of cortical dynamics during gait adaptation.
datasets.authors: Johanna Wagner, Ramon Martinez-Cancino, Scott Makeig, Arnaud Delorme, Christa Neuper, Teodoro Solis-Escalante, Gernot Mueller-Putz

datasets.name: RS_TMSEEG_Data
datasets.description: This dataset contains transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) combined with electroencephalography (EEG) recordings acquired to identify site- and stimulation-specific TMS-evoked potentials. It accompanies a study that applied a quantitative cosine similarity metric to distinguish TMS-evoked EEG responses across stimulation sites and conditions. The data are mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro (ds001849).
datasets.authors: Michael Freedberg, Jack A. Reeves, Sara J. Hussain, Kareem A. Zaghloul, Eric M. Wassermann

datasets.name: EEG study of the attentional blink; before, during, and after transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (tDCS)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from participants performing an attentional blink task before, during, and after transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS). Each participant visited the lab twice, receiving anodal or cathodal stimulation over F3 with a return electrode over the right forehead, with complete data for 40 participants. The dataset supports study of concurrent tDCS-EEG artifacts and of stimulation effects on attentional blink event-related responses.
datasets.authors: Leon C. Reteig, Lionel A. Newman, K. Richard Ridderinkhof, Heleen A. Slagter
datasets.eeg_reference: CMS, placed in CMS slot of Biosemi cap

datasets.name: Evidence accumulation relates to perceptual consciousness and monitoring
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 20 healthy participants performing a tactile detection task with confidence ratings, plus ECoG from one patient with intractable epilepsy. The data were collected to study how evidence accumulation relates to perceptual consciousness and metacognitive monitoring. Near-threshold vibrotactile stimuli were delivered to the right wrist, with detection and confidence reports collected over 500 trials per participant.
datasets.authors: Michael Pereira, Pierre Mégevand, Mi Xue Tan, Wenwen Chang, Shuo Wang, Ali Rezai, Margitta Seeck, Marco Corniola, Shahan Momjian, Fosco Bernasconi, Olaf Blanke, Nathan Faivre

datasets.name: Implicit Learning EEG (BioSemi)
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings acquired with a BioSemi system in an implicit learning paradigm. It is organized according to the EEG-BIDS specification and was prepared with MNE-BIDS. The data are shared as a raw BIDS dataset under a CC0 license.
datasets.authors: Mateo Leganes-Fonteneau

datasets.name: EEG data offline and online during motor imagery for standing and sitting
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 32 participants performing motor imagery of sit-to-stand and stand-to-sit movements, collected in offline and online brain-computer interface (BCI) phases. Signals were recorded from 17 channels (10-20 placement) at 250 Hz while visual cues on a screen guided motor imagery and idle-state trials. Offline data were used to train machine learning models that then provided real-time task detection in the online phase.
datasets.authors: Nayid Triana-Guzman, Alvaro D Orjuela-Cañon, Andres L Jutinico, Omar Mendoza-Montoya, Javier M Antelis

datasets.name: MEG-BIDS OMEGA RestingState_sample
datasets.description: A sample resting-state MEG dataset from the Open MEG Archive (OMEGA), containing 5-minute eyes-open recordings from five subjects. Data were acquired at the Montreal Neurological Institute with a 275-channel CTF MEG system and include head shape digitization and defaced structural T1 images processed with FreeSurfer. The dataset is organized according to the MEG-BIDS specification.
datasets.authors: Guiomar Niso, Jeremy Moreau, Elizabeth Bock, Francois Tadel, Sylvain Baillet

datasets.name: MEG-BIDS Brainstorm data sample
datasets.description: A single-subject auditory evoked field MEG dataset in BIDS format, recorded at the Montreal Neurological Institute with a CTF 275 system. The subject listened binaurally to regular and deviant beeps and pressed a button for deviants. Two 6-minute task runs, an empty-room recording, head shape digitization and anatomical MRI are included. It was originally created as a tutorial dataset for the Brainstorm software.
datasets.authors: Elizabeth Bock, Peter Donhauser, Francois Tadel, Guiomar Niso, Sylvain Baillet

datasets.name: 39 By BP
datasets.description: EEG recordings from participants receiving laser stimuli of calibrated intensity to evoke pain. After individual calibration to the energy level yielding an average rating of 7, each participant received 10 laser stimulations and rated pain intensity and unpleasantness on a 0-10 numeric rating scale. The dataset supports research on pain perception and related neural responses.
datasets.authors: Zhao Xiangyue, Zhou Jingyao, Zhang Libo, Duan Haoqing, Wei Shiyu, Bi Yanzhi, Hu Li

datasets.name:
A Human EEG
Dataset for Multisensory Perception and Mental
Imagery
datasets.description: The YOTO (You Only Think Once) dataset is a human EEG resource for studying multisensory perception and mental imagery. Twenty participants completed tasks with unimodal and multimodal (visual, auditory, and combined) cues while EEG was recorded at 1000 Hz, and they gave self-reported vividness ratings of their imagery. Technical validation with event-related potentials and power spectral density analyses confirmed data reliability and distinct neural responses across stimuli, supporting research on neural decoding, perception, and cognitive modeling.
datasets.authors: Yan-Han Chang, Hsi-An Chen, Min-Jiun Tsai, Chun-Lung Tseng, Ching-Huei Lo, Kuan-Chih Huang, Chun-Shu Wei

datasets.name: Very-High-Density Diffuse Optical Tomography System Validation Dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains paired very high-density diffuse optical tomography (VHD-DOT) and fMRI recordings from 8 participants performing functional localizer and movie-viewing tasks. VHD-DOT data are stored in SNIRF format in the first two sessions per subject, while later sessions hold fMRI data in NIfTI format. Preprocessed fMRI data used for comparison with VHD-DOT are provided in the derivatives folder, supporting validation of whole-head optical brain mapping.
datasets.authors: Morgan Fogarty, Sean M. Rafferty, Zachary E. Markow, Anthony C. O’Sullivan, Calamity F. Svoboda, Tessa George, Kelsey King, Dana Wilhelm, Kalyan Tripathy, Emily M. Mugler, Stephanie Naufel, Allen Yin, Jason W. Trobaugh, Adam T. Eggebrecht, Edward J. Richter, Joseph P. Culver

datasets.name: Nejedly-2020b-multicenter-10.1038/s41597-020-0532-5
datasets.description: This dataset provides intracranial EEG (stereo-EEG) clips from a multicenter collection used for classifying physiological and pathological graphoelements and artifactual signals. It contains independent 3 s single-channel clips sampled at 5000 Hz, converted to BIDS from the segmented .mat archives released with the original publication. Events preserve clip labels, anatomy, seizure onset zone flags, reviewer identity, and electrode type.
datasets.authors: Petr Nejedly, Vaclav Kremen, Vladimir Sladky, Jan Cimbalnik, Petr Klimes, Filip Plesinger, Filip Mivalt, Vojtech Travnicek, Ivo Viscor, Martin Pail, Josef Halamek, Benjamin Brinkmann, Milan Brazdil, Pavel Jurak, Gregory Worrell

datasets.name: Nejedly-2020a-multicenter-10.1038/s41597-020-0532-5
datasets.description: This dataset provides multicenter intracranial EEG (iEEG) clips for classification of physiological and pathological graphoelements and artifactual signals. It was converted to BIDS from the public segmented .mat archives released with Nejedly et al. 2020. Each run concatenates independent 3 s single-channel clips from one subject and one SEEG contact sampled at 5000 Hz, with events preserving labels, anatomy, reviewer ID, SOZ flag, and electrode type.
datasets.authors: Petr Nejedly, Vaclav Kremen, Vladimir Sladky, Jan Cimbalnik, Petr Klimes, Filip Plesinger, Filip Mivalt, Vojtech Travnicek, Ivo Viscor, Martin Pail, Josef Halamek, Benjamin Brinkmann, Milan Brazdil, Pavel Jurak, Gregory Worrell

datasets.description: The MNE-Sample-Data dataset is a simultaneous MEG and 60-channel EEG recording with an accompanying structural MRI, distributed with the MNE software. Checkerboard patterns were presented to the left and right visual fields, interleaved with tones to the left or right ear, and the subject responded to occasional smiley faces. It serves as a standard example dataset for demonstrating MEG/EEG analysis workflows, and FreeSurfer-derived anatomical surfaces are included.
datasets.authors: Alexandre Gramfort, Matti S Hämäläinen

datasets.name: A dataset of EEG recordings from: Alzheimer's disease, Frontotemporal dementia and Healthy subjects
datasets.description: Resting-state, eyes-closed scalp EEG recordings from 88 participants: 36 with Alzheimer's disease, 23 with frontotemporal dementia, and 29 healthy controls. Recordings were acquired in routine clinical conditions with a 19-electrode 10-20 montage, and cognitive status was assessed with the MMSE. The dataset includes raw recordings and preprocessed, denoised derivatives, supporting research on EEG-based dementia detection and classification.
datasets.authors: Andreas Miltiadous, Katerina D. Tzimourta, Theodora Afrantou, Panagiotis Ioannidis, Nikolaos Grigoriadis, Dimitrios G. Tsalikakis, Pantelis Angelidis, Markos G. Tsipouras, Evripidis Glavas, Nikolaos Giannakeas, Alexandros T. Tzallas

datasets.name: Subjective tinnitus severity correlates with objective changes in human auditory cortex as measured by functional near-infrared spectroscopy
datasets.description: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) recordings of human auditory cortex from participants with subjective tinnitus and matched controls. The dataset supports investigation of whether subjective tinnitus severity relates to objective hemodynamic changes in auditory cortex. Data were acquired with a NIRx NIRSport2 system and organized in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Gopika Satish, Leah M. Taylor, Megan P. Arnold, Julia Gallagher-Shale, Karthikeyan Krishnamurthy, Gregory J. Basura

datasets.name: Narrative Reward
datasets.description: EEG dataset from forty participants who read an interactive story containing decision points. On each trial participants saw an item, made a yes/no decision, and received correct or incorrect feedback. The design compares a narrative condition, with story context at item onset and after feedback, against a nonnarrative condition with no such context. It is intended for studying how narrative context affects reward and feedback processing.
datasets.authors: Stacey-Jane Harris, Cameron D. Hassall

datasets.name: Auditory Streaming and Interoception
datasets.description: EEG dataset on auditory streaming and interoception, collected at the University of Chicago by Veillette, Joshi, Li, and Nusbaum. Data are organized in BIDS format (BrainVision files) and released under a CC0 license.
datasets.authors: John Veillette, Aditi Joshi, Ying Li, Howard Nusbaum

datasets.name: Auditory Streaming and Interoception
datasets.description: EEG dataset on auditory streaming and interoception, collected at the University of Chicago and organized in BIDS format. The README gives few details of the experimental design, so the description rests mainly on the dataset name and metadata.
datasets.authors: John Veillette, Aditi Joshi, Ying Li, Howard Nusbaum

datasets.name: Placebo Neuroepo multisession Phase II and III
datasets.description: Multisession EEG dataset from a randomized, placebo-controlled study of intranasal NeuroEPO (erythropoietin-derived formulation) in patients with Parkinson's disease. Clinical (MDS-UPDRS III) and EEG assessments were acquired at baseline and 9 months after completing the intervention. Cumulative NeuroEPO dose is coded per participant (placebo = 0), enabling analysis of treatment effects on brain activity.
datasets.authors: Maria Luisa Bringas Vega, Lilia Morales Chacon, Ivonne Pedroso Ibanez

datasets.name: Neuroepo multisession Phase II and III
datasets.description: Multisession EEG and clinical dataset from a randomized, placebo-controlled study of intranasal NeuroEPO (an erythropoietin formulation) in patients with Parkinson's disease. Participants were assessed at baseline and 9 months after the intervention, with cumulative NeuroEPO dose quantified and placebo coded as zero. The dataset supports analysis of treatment exposure, EEG-derived measures, and motor outcomes (MDS-UPDRS III).
datasets.authors: Maria Luisa Bringas Vega, Lilia Morales Chacon, Ivonne Pedroso Ibanez

datasets.name: Prisoner's Dilemma EEG Dataset
datasets.description: An EEG-BIDS dataset from a three-person hyperscanning experiment in which participants played a prisoner's dilemma game. It includes 11 triads (3 participants each), with recordings across decision, feedback, and rest tasks. Behavioral labels are provided in the events files, and EEG data are stored in EEGLAB .set format.
datasets.authors: n/a

datasets.name: Whole-Head Cocktail Party fNIRS
datasets.description: Whole-head functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) recordings from 38 participants performing covert and overt spatial-attention tasks in a cocktail-party paradigm, with simultaneous eye tracking. The montage comprises 56 sources and 144 detectors, yielding 1134 measurement channels sampled at about 8.99 Hz. Tasks include overt and covert attention, a visual orienting baseline, resting state, and video-locked attention recordings.
datasets.authors: Sudan Duwadi, De'Ja Rogers, Alex D. Boyd, Laura B. Carlton, Yiwen Zhang, Anna Kawai Gaona, Aneesa Diya Pathiyaparambath, Ravin Chaudhury, Bernhard B Zimmermann, Walker J O'Brien, Alexander von Lühmann, David A. Boas, Meryem A. Yücel, Kamal Sen

datasets.name: Perturbed beam-walking task
datasets.description: This dataset contains synchronized 128-channel EEG, lower leg and neck EMG, EOG, and motion capture recordings from participants standing or walking on a treadmill-mounted balance beam while receiving sensorimotor perturbations. Perturbations were either virtual-reality visual field rotations or side-to-side waist pulls, delivered across four 10-minute sessions with 150 perturbations each. The data support study of electrocortical and muscular responses to balance perturbations during walking and standing.
datasets.authors: Steven Peterson, Daniel Ferris

datasets.name: BCI-FIT: A customization protocol for communication brain-computer interface systems.
datasets.description: EEG recordings from five participants with speech and/or physical impairments due to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) who used a non-implantable communication brain-computer interface (cBCI) over multiple visits. Participants completed calibration and copy-spelling tasks with Matrix and RSVP layouts, in both customized and non-customized system configurations. Customization was iteratively adjusted based on typing performance, preferences, clinical observations, brain signal characteristics, and offline simulations. The data are organized in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Betts Peters, Daniel Klee, Michelle Kinsella, Yonah Hendin, Tab Memmott, Matthew Lawhead, Srikar Ananthoju, Basak Celik, Scott Spaulding, Barry Oken, Melanie Fried-Oken
datasets.eeg_reference: Averaged linked-ear reference: (A1 + A2) / 2, with active common-mode follower

datasets.name: Cambridge_data_resting
datasets.description: Resting-state functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) recordings from the Cambridge_data_resting dataset, originally deposited on OpenNeuro (ds007719) by Emilia Butters and mirrored on NEMAR. The dataset is organized according to BIDS and contains 66 files (about 8.62 GB) of continuous fNIRS data in SNIRF format, with accompanying JSON and TSV sidecar files describing channels, optodes, and events. Detailed information on participants, acquisition hardware, and experimental protocol is not provided in the available documentation.
datasets.authors: Enter author names here

datasets.name: Cambridge_data
datasets.description: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) dataset named Cambridge_data, deposited on OpenNeuro (ds007714) by Gemma Bale and colleagues and mirrored on NEMAR. The data are organized in BIDS format as SNIRF recordings with accompanying JSON and TSV metadata files (65 files, about 1.24 GB). The source deposit does not document the experimental paradigm, participant characteristics, or recording setup, so these details should be obtained from the original authors.
datasets.authors: Enter author names here

datasets.name: The Temporal Sequence of Party Leader Incongruence
datasets.description: High-density 64-channel EEG and linked behavioral data from 44 Dutch participants in a preregistered study of how partisans process political incongruence. Two tasks separate identity incongruence (Just Faces) from source-content incongruence (Statements & Faces), using supporters of GreenLeft/Labour as the in-party group and the far-right PVV as the out-party group. The dataset tests the 'Hot Cognition' hypothesis by examining the temporal sequence of neural responses to party leaders and their messages.
datasets.authors: Gustavo Couto de Jesus, Bert N. Bakker, Gijs Schumacher, Joe Bathelt

datasets.name: TimeSeries BIDS converted
datasets.description: A functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) time-series dataset converted to BIDS format from a MATLAB file containing hemoglobin concentration time series (HbO) from 18 subjects across two sessions, with ICA-based denoising applied. The dataset is a BIDS conversion of an original deposit and includes NIRS recordings and associated metadata.
datasets.authors: Niu，Haijing, Zheng, Sha, Yuan, Haodong

datasets.name: High-Density Diffuse Optical Tomography Audiovisual Movie Viewing Dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains high-density diffuse optical tomography (HD-DOT) recordings from five adult participants completing functional localizer and naturalistic audiovisual movie viewing tasks. Data are stored in SNIRF format together with optode and landmark locations linked to subject-specific head models. Metadata describing the movie clips used as stimuli (20 clips from Finding Nemo, Frozen, Moana, Curious George and Daniel Tiger's Neighborhood) are provided, although the commercial media files are not included. Note: participant A04 has 16 additional movie-labelled runs (ses-7 MOV002-MOV009 and ses-8 MOV001-MOV008) that are not part of the 40 A04 movie runs in the 2024 paper and are not listed in the run-to-clip table. They likely correspond to a control experiment described in the 2025 Neurophotonics paper (audio-only and silent-video clips), but the stimulus condition of each session has not been confirmed by the authors, so these runs should not be assumed to be audiovisual movie viewing. Known file issues: events.tsv onset and duration are given in samples (10.42 Hz) rather than seconds, and the SNIRF files fail to load with mne.io.read_raw_snirf because landmarkLabels is stored as a 2-D array.
datasets.authors: Morgan Fogarty, Kalyan Tripathy, Alexandra M Svoboda, Mariel L Schroeder, Sean M Rafferty, Edward J Richter, Christopher Tracy, Patricia K Mansfield, Madison Booth, Andrew K Fishell, Arefeh Sherafati, Zachary E Markow, Muriah D Wheelock, Ana Maria Arbelaez, Bradley L Schlaggar, Christopher D Smyser, Adam T Eggebrecht, Joseph P Culver

datasets.name: A Light Weight Multi-Distance fNIRS Dataset for Ball-Squeezing Task and Purposeful Motion Artifact Creation Task
datasets.description: A multi-distance, high-density fNIRS dataset recorded over the motor cortex with a lightweight system that includes an accelerometer. Participants completed a resting-state recording, a bilateral ball-squeezing task, and a motion creation task with instructed head and facial movements to deliberately induce motion artifacts. The dataset supports work on short-separation regression, motion artifact correction, and diffuse optical tomography image reconstruction.
datasets.authors: Gao, Yuanyuan, Rogers, De’Ja, von Lühmann, Alexander, Ortega-Martinez, Antonio, Boas, David, Yücel, Meryem

datasets.name: ball_squeeze_2025
datasets.description: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) dataset named ball_squeeze_2025, in BIDS format with SNIRF recordings (68 files, approximately 5.42 GB). The dataset title suggests a ball-squeezing motor task, but the source README does not describe the experimental paradigm, participants, or acquisition parameters. The BIDS metadata lists Boston University IRB approval 4502. The dataset is mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro (ds006903).
datasets.authors: Enter author names here

datasets.name: Profound neuronal differences during Exercise-Induced Hypoalgesia between athletes and non-athletes revealed by functional near-infrared spectroscopy
datasets.description: This fNIRS dataset captures brain oxygenation changes during exercise-induced hypoalgesia in 22 endurance athletes and 20 non-athletes. Participants completed high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and pressure pain tests while oxyhemoglobin was recorded over the prefrontal, sensorimotor and posterior parietal cortices. The data support comparisons of athlete and non-athlete neural responses to exercise and pain, and how these relate to pain perception.
datasets.authors: Maria Geisler, Marco Herbsleb, Feliberto de la Cruz, Sabrina von Au, Andy Schumann, Ilona Croy, Karl-Jürgen Bär

datasets.name: ball_squeeze_Carlton_2025
datasets.description: A high-density functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) dataset recorded during a ball-squeezing motor task at Boston University. The recordings were used to develop and optimize surface-based image reconstruction methods for high-density fNIRS. The dataset is mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro (ds006673).
datasets.authors: Laura B. Carlton, Miray Altinkaynak, Shannon Kelley, Bernhard Zimmerman, Sreekanth Kura, Eike Middell, Alexander von Luhmann, Meryem A. Yucel, David A. Boas

datasets.name: Reliability-Dubois2024
datasets.description: Time-domain functional near-infrared spectroscopy (TD-fNIRS) recordings collected with the Kernel system to assess the reliability of brain metrics derived from this device. The dataset accompanies a Scientific Reports study evaluating the test-retest reliability of TD-fNIRS measures. It is mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro (ds006545).
datasets.authors: Kernel

datasets.name: HeartBEAM: Older Adult Resting State and Auditory Oddball Task EEG Data
datasets.description: EEG recordings from older adults during eyes-open and eyes-closed resting state and during passive and active auditory oddball tasks. Each participant was recorded under a control condition and an arousal condition induced by the threat of unpredictable shock. The data come from the HeartBEAM study and support research on locus coeruleus-noradrenaline system activity and arousal in aging.
datasets.authors: Andy Jeesu Kim, Santiago Morales, Joshua Senior, Mara Mather

datasets.name: High-DensityvSparsefNIRS_WordColorStroop_HD_Anderson_2025
datasets.description: This dataset contains high-density, multi-distance functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) recordings collected while participants performed a word-color Stroop task. It was designed to compare high-density with sparse fNIRS measurement configurations for detecting task-related brain activity. The data are organized in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Jessica E. Anderson, Laura Carlton, Sreekanth Kura, Walker J. O'Brien, De'Ja Rogers, Parisa Rahimi, Parya Y. Farzam, Muhammad H. Zaman, David A. Boas, Meryem A. Yücel

datasets.name: High-DensityvSparsefNIRS_WordColorStroop_Sparse_Anderson_2025
datasets.description: This dataset contains functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) recordings collected during a word-color Stroop task using a sparse fNIRS montage. It accompanies a study comparing high-density, multi-distance fNIRS with sparse configurations for detecting task-related brain activity. The data are organized in BIDS format and are mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro.
datasets.authors: Jessica E. Anderson, Laura Carlton, Sreekanth Kura, Walker J. O'Brien, De'Ja Rogers, Parisa Rahimi, Parya Y. Farzam, Muhammad H. Zaman, David A. Boas, Meryem A. Yücel

datasets.name: Cueing the future to reduce temporal discounting
datasets.description: EEG dataset investigating whether episodic future thinking can reduce temporal discounting. Participants described a series of personal future events and were then cued to think about these events while making intertemporal choices. They also rated the vividness of their mental imagery for each event.
datasets.authors: Isaac Kinley, Sue Becker

datasets.name: InclusionStudy
datasets.description: This dataset contains functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) recordings collected to quantify how hair and skin characteristics affect fNIRS signal quality. It was collected to support more inclusive fNIRS research and device design. The data are organized in BIDS format and mirrored from OpenNeuro.
datasets.authors: Meryem A. Yücel, Jessica E. Anderson, De'Ja Rogers, Parisa Hajirahimi, Parya Farzam, Yuanyuan Gao, Rini I. Kaplan, Emily J. Braun, Nishaat Mukadam, Sudan Duwadi, Laura Carlton, David Beeler, Lindsay K. Butler, Erin Carpenter, Jaimie Girnis, John Wilson, Vaibhav Tripathi, Yiwen Zhang, Bettina Sorger, Alexander von Lühmann, David C. Somers, Alice Cronin-Golomb, Swathi Kiran, Terry D. Ellis, David A. Boas

datasets.name: Memory Reactivation Levels Remain Unaffected by Anticipated Interference
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a visual working memory interference task (Experiment 1) investigating whether memory reactivation levels are affected by anticipated interference. Participants memorized a cued target object among two lateral objects; interference objects were shown in half of the blocks, followed by a probe and feedback. Preprocessing steps are described in an accompanying preprint and OSF repository referenced by the dataset authors.
datasets.authors: xx

datasets.name: FRESH Audio Dataset
datasets.description: The FRESH Audio Dataset is a functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) dataset in BIDS format, collected with auditory stimulation. It was contributed by Robert Luke, Maureen Shader and David McAlpine and is also available through OpenNeuro. The README gives no further detail, and an accompanying publication is noted as in preparation.
datasets.authors: Robert Luke, Maureen Shader, David McAlpine

datasets.name: FRESH Motor Dataset
datasets.description: The FRESH Motor Dataset is a functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) dataset organized in BIDS format. It is associated with a motor task paradigm. The README gives little detail, and the record is a NEMAR-hosted version of the OpenNeuro deposit ds005963.
datasets.authors: Rickson C. Mesquita

datasets.name: Mirror Neuron Study
datasets.description: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) dataset from a mirror neuron study examining brain correlates of motor complexity during observed and executed actions. The recordings were collected at Boston University and are shared in BIDS format, mirrored from OpenNeuro.
datasets.authors: Xinge Li, Manon A. Krol, Sahar Jahani, David A. Boas, Helen Tager-Flusberg, Meryem A. Yücel

datasets.name: Motion-Yucel2014
datasets.description: This dataset contains functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) recordings collected to evaluate motion artifacts in long-term clinical NIRS monitoring. It accompanies a study comparing collodion-fixed prism-based optical fibers with conventional fiber attachment for reducing motion artifacts. The data are mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro.
datasets.authors: Yücel, Meryem, Selb, Juliette, Boas, David, Cash, Sydney, Cooper, Robert

datasets.name: Real-time personalized brain state-dependent TMS in healthy adults
datasets.description: This dataset contains raw EEG and transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) data from healthy adults, collected to test real-time, personalized brain state-dependent stimulation. Whole-brain activity patterns were decoded in real time to predict activation of the corticospinal tract, with motor evoked potentials as the outcome measure. The companion publication (Khatri, Pulliam, Manesiya, Cortez, Millán and Hussain, 'Personalized whole-brain activity patterns predict human corticospinal tract activation in real-time', Brain Stimulation, 2024) is in press and has no DOI yet.
datasets.authors: Uttara Khatri, Sara Hussain

datasets.name: Electrical_Morphine_Placebo_2018
datasets.description: This fNIRS (functional near-infrared spectroscopy) dataset examines how morphine affects cortical hemodynamic responses to painful electrical stimulation compared with placebo. Recordings target the medial frontopolar cortex (medial BA 10) in healthy participants. The dataset supports research on objective, neuroimaging-based markers of analgesic drug effects.
datasets.authors: Peng, Ke, Yücel, Meryem, Steele, Sarah, Bittner, Edward, Aasted, Christopher, Hoeft, Mark, Lee, Arielle, George, Edward, Boas, David, Becerra, Lino, Borsook, David

datasets.name: Electrical_Thermal_FingerTapping_2015
datasets.description: A functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) dataset of hemodynamic brain responses to electrical and thermal painful stimuli and to a finger-tapping task. It was collected to examine the specificity of cortical hemodynamic responses to pain and to support evaluation of short-separation regression for separating systemic autonomic effects from cerebral responses.
datasets.authors: Yücel, Meryem, Selb, Juliette, Aasted, Christopher, Petkov, Mihayl, Borsook, David, Boas, David, Becerra, Lino

datasets.name: illusory-face-eeg
datasets.description: EEG dataset investigating the neural time course of spontaneous face perception, including face pareidolia. Participants viewed 300 images of human faces, illusory faces, and matched non-face objects presented centrally at 3.75 Hz while performing an orthogonal target detection task. The study also involved behavioural tasks (odd-one-out dissimilarity, face-likeness ratings, and face/object categorisation) using the same stimuli.
datasets.authors: Amanda K Robinson, Greta Stuart, Sophia M Shatek, Adrian Herbert, Jessica Taubert

datasets.name: 29 By BP
datasets.description: EEG dataset '29 By BP' collected by Zhao Xiangyue, Hu Li and colleagues, relating to research on human brain responses to nociceptive stimulation, in particular concomitant activation of Aδ and C nociceptors. The associated publication (Hu et al., 2014, J Neurosci) investigates EEG responses to concomitant stimulation of Aδ and C nociceptors. The dataset is shared under a CC0 license.
datasets.authors: Zhao Xiangyue, Zhou Jingyao, Zhang Libo, Duan Haoqing, Wei Shiyu, Bi Yanzhi, Hu Li

datasets.name: Le Petit Prince (LPP) Multi-talker: Naturalistic 7T fMRI and EEG Dataset
datasets.description: A naturalistic multi-talker listening dataset in which 25 native Mandarin speakers underwent both 7T fMRI and 64-channel EEG while listening to the Chinese version of Le Petit Prince. Conditions included single-talker and mixed-talker speech with attention directed to different talkers, with comprehension quizzes after each run. The dataset supports research on speech perception, selective attention, and language processing under naturalistic conditions.
datasets.authors: Zhengwu Ma, Nan Wang, Jixing Li

datasets.name: 142 by Biosemi
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 142 participants who received laser-evoked pain stimuli at fixed low and high intensities and rated the pain intensity after each stimulus. Each participant completed 3 blocks of 10 stimuli, with high and low pain stimuli evenly distributed within each block. Data were recorded with a Biosemi system and are intended for studying the neural correlates of pain perception.
datasets.authors: Zhao Xiangyue, Zhou Jingyao, Zhang Libo, Duan Haoqing, Wei Shiyu, Bi Yanzhi, Hu Li

datasets.name: 65 By ANT
datasets.description: EEG dataset recorded from participants receiving laser stimulation and verbally rating the resulting pain intensity. After an initial calibration to find the energy level producing an average rating of 7, each participant received 30 laser stimuli and rated each one on a 0-10 scale, from no sensation to unbearable pain.
datasets.authors: Zhao Xiangyue, Zhou Jingyao, Zhang Libo, Duan Haoqing, Wei Shiyu, Bi Yanzhi, Hu Li

datasets.name: 30 By ANT
datasets.description: EEG recordings from participants receiving a series of laser stimuli while rating pain intensity. After an initial calibration to find the laser energy that yielded an average rating of 7, each participant received 30 laser stimuli and verbally rated each one on a 0-10 pain scale. The dataset supports research on the neural correlates of pain perception.
datasets.authors: Zhao Xiangyue, Zhou Jingyao, Zhang Libo, Duan Haoqing, Wei Shiyu, Bi Yanzhi, Hu Li

datasets.name: 29 By ANT
datasets.description: An EEG dataset of participants receiving laser stimuli at low and high intensities while rating perceived pain on a 0-10 scale. Each participant completed 4 blocks of 40 trials (160 stimulations in total), with half of the trials at high intensity and half at low intensity. The dataset supports research on pain perception and laser-evoked brain responses.
datasets.authors: Zhao Xiangyue, Zhou Jingyao, Zhang Libo, Duan Haoqing, Wei Shiyu, Bi Yanzhi, Hu Li

datasets.name: 26 By Biosemi
datasets.description: EEG dataset recorded with a Biosemi system from participants receiving laser stimulation to elicit pain. After the laser intensity was calibrated to an average rating of about 7 on a 0-10 scale, each participant received 16 fixed-intensity laser stimuli roughly 20 seconds apart and rated the pain intensity after each one. The dataset supports research on pain perception and laser-evoked brain responses.
datasets.authors: Zhao Xiangyue, Zhou Jingyao, Zhang Libo, Duan Haoqing, Wei Shiyu, Bi Yanzhi, Hu Li

datasets.name: 223 By BP
datasets.description: EEG dataset recorded while participants received laser-evoked pain stimuli at fixed intensities (3/3.5 J for low pain and 3.5/4 J for high pain). Each participant completed three blocks of ten stimuli, with high and low pain intensities evenly distributed within each block. After each stimulus, participants rated pain intensity on a 0-10 scale.
datasets.authors: Zhao Xiangyue, Zhou Jingyao, Zhang Libo, Duan Haoqing, Wei Shiyu, Bi Yanzhi, Hu Li

datasets.name: AMRI 16-N-0031 sleep1
datasets.description: Overnight simultaneous EEG-fMRI recordings from a pilot sleep study (sleep1) conducted at the Advanced MRI section of NINDS, NIH, around 2016-2017. Subjects were scanned for approximately 8 hours across two consecutive nights and were aroused at random intervals eight times per night. The dataset is the pilot for the later sleep2 study.
datasets.authors: Picchioni, Dante, Duyn, Jeff H, de Zwart, Jacco A

datasets.name: An fNIRS dataset for driving risk cognition of passengers in highly automated driving scenarios
datasets.description: This dataset contains functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) recordings of prefrontal cortex activity from 20 participants (ages 21-46; 5 female, 15 male) in a driving simulator. Participants experienced fourteen types of highly automated driving scenarios, and the dataset accompanies scenario data and subjective danger ratings. It is intended to support study of prefrontal activity differences between low-risk and high-risk driving episodes, with potential application to brain-computer interfaces and improving safety of the intended functionality (SOTIF).
datasets.authors: Xiaofei Zhang , Qiaoya Wang , Jun Li, Xiaorong Gao , Bowen Li , Bingbing Nie , Jianqiang Wang , Ziyuan Zhou , Yingkai Yang , Hong Wang

datasets.name: Spatial Attention Decoding using fNIRS During Complex Scene Analysis
datasets.description: This dataset contains functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) recordings collected while participants performed spatial attention tasks during complex auditory scene analysis. It supports research on decoding the focus of spatial attention from hemodynamic signals. The data are organized in BIDS format and accompany a published data paper.
datasets.authors: Matthew Ning, Sudan Duwadi, Meryem A. Yucel, Alexander Von Luhmann, David A. Boas, Kamal Sen

datasets.name: Mobile EEG split-belt walking study
datasets.description: Mobile brain/body imaging (MoBI) dataset of scalp EEG recorded during split-belt treadmill walking to study cortical activity related to locomotor adaptation. Thirty participants completed abrupt and gradual split-belt walking paradigms with a 2:1 belt speed ratio.
datasets.authors: Noelle A. Jacobsen, Daniel P. Ferris

datasets.name: Meta-rdk: Raw EEG data
datasets.description: Raw EEG recordings from 20 individuals with a schizophrenia spectrum disorder and 22 healthy control participants performing a random-dot motion discrimination task. After each left/right decision, participants rated their confidence on a visual analog scale. The dataset supports investigation of perceptual decision-making and metacognition in schizophrenia.
datasets.authors: Martin Rouy, Matthieu Roger, Dorian Goueytes, Michael Pereira, Paul Roux, Nathan Faivre

datasets.name: HUP iEEG Epilepsy Dataset
datasets.description: De-identified intracranial EEG recordings from 58 patients undergoing surgical evaluation for drug-resistant epilepsy at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania. Recordings used subdural grid, strip, and depth electrodes (ECoG) or stereotactically placed depth electrodes (SEEG), and include interictal and ictal periods. The dataset provides electrode localizations in ICBM152 MNI space, clinically determined seizure onset channels, and channels overlapping the resection or ablation zone segmented from the resection cavity.
datasets.authors: John M. Bernabei, Adam Li, Andrew Y. Revell, Rachel J. Smith, Kristin M. Gunnarsdottir, Ian Z. Ong, Kathryn A. Davis, Nishant Sinha, Sridevi Sarma, Brian Litt

datasets.name: The nature of neural object representations during dynamic occlusion
datasets.description: Raw and preprocessed magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from participants viewing objects that moved along trajectories and were either occluded or disappeared. The dataset supports investigation of how the brain represents objects during dynamic occlusion. It includes behavioural and eye-tracking data as source data, and preprocessed epochs in CoSMoMVPA format.
datasets.authors: Lina Teichmann, Denise Moerel, Anina Rich, Chris Baker

datasets.name: Cattan, Rodrigues & Congedo 2019 — Passive Head-Mounted Display Music-Listening EEG dataset (PHMD)
datasets.description: This dataset contains 16-channel electroencephalographic recordings from 12 healthy participants who listened to harpsichord music while fixating on a visual marker, with and without a passive head-mounted display (a headset containing no electronics apart from a smartphone). Each participant completed ten one-minute eyes-open blocks, five with the smartphone switched on and five with it switched off, in randomized order. The data were collected in a pilot experiment at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble, in 2017 to assess the impact of passive VR headsets on EEG signal quality.
datasets.authors: G. Cattan, P. L. C. Rodrigues, M. Congedo

datasets.name: 7-day motor imagery BCI EEG dataset from Zhou et al 2021
datasets.description: A longitudinal EEG dataset of motor imagery brain-computer interface (BCI) recordings from 20 healthy participants, each recorded over 7 separate days without feedback training. Participants imagined left-hand, right-hand and both-feet movements, or rested, in response to visual arrow cues. Recordings were made at 500 Hz with a 41-electrode or 26-electrode Neuroscan cap plus EOG channels. This version is a BIDS-formatted derivative regenerated through MOABB with corrected channel names and montage.
datasets.authors: Qing Zhou, Jiafan Lin, Lin Yao, Yueming Wang, Yan Han, Kedi Xu

datasets.name: Langer et al. 2017 — Multimodal Resource for Studying Information Processing in the Developing Brain (MIPDB)
datasets.description: The Multimodal Resource for Studying Information Processing in the Developing Brain (MIPDB) contains high-density EEG and eye-tracking recordings from 111 participants in a developmental cohort spanning childhood to adulthood. Participants completed a battery of cognitive and perceptual paradigms: resting state, surround suppression, naturalistic viewing, contrast change detection, sequence learning, and symbol search. The resource supports research on the maturation of information processing in the human brain. This BIDS conversion publishes each recording block as a separate task.
datasets.authors: Nicolas Langer, Erica J Ho, Lindsay M Alexander, Helen Y Xu, Renee K Jozanovic, Simon Henin, Agustin Petroni, Samantha Cohen, Enitan T Marcelle, Lucas C Parra, Michael P Milham, Simon P Kelly

datasets.name: He-2025-vocalmind-10.1038/s41597-025-04741-2
datasets.description: VocalMind is a stereotactic EEG (sEEG) dataset for speech decoding research in a tonal language, Mandarin Chinese. Intracranial recordings were acquired during vocalized, mimed, and imagined speech, supporting work on speech brain-computer interfaces and neural decoding of overt and covert speech. This BIDS iEEG conversion currently contains one subject, with a separate task for each speech mode.
datasets.authors: Tianyu He, Mingyi Wei, Ruicong Wang, Renzhi Wang, Shiwei Du, Siqi Cai, Wei Tao, Haizhou Li

datasets.name: Chang et al. 2025 — A multi-paradigm EEG dataset for studying upper limb rehabilitation exercises (Lanzhou Jiaotong University)
datasets.description: This dataset contains scalp EEG recordings from 28 participants performing or imagining upper-limb rehabilitation exercises under a multi-paradigm protocol. It is intended to support research on motor-imagery and rehabilitation brain-computer interfaces for restoring upper-limb function. The data are organized in BIDS format under a motor-imagery task.
datasets.authors: Wenwen Chang, Weixuan Kong, Guanghui Yan, Renjie Lv, Kaiyue Du, Muhammad Tariq Sadiq, Bin Guo, Rong Yin, Xuan Liu

datasets.name: The Brain, Body, and Behaviour Dataset (1.0.0) - Experiment 1
datasets.description: Eye-tracking data from 27 participants who watched five educational videos in two sessions: an attentive condition, in which participants were tested afterward with multiple-choice questions, and a distracted condition, in which they silently counted backwards. The dataset includes gaze, pupil size, blinks, saccades and fixations, plus questionnaires with domain and memory questions. It is Experiment 1 of the Brain, Body, and Behavior Dataset (BBBD) and supports research on attention and learning from video.
datasets.authors: Jens Madsen, Nikhil Kuppa, Lucas Parra

datasets.name: The Brain, Body, and Behaviour Dataset (1.0.0) - Experiment 4
datasets.description: Multimodal recordings from 43 participants who watched short educational videos in two sessions: first in an attentive condition and then again in a distracted condition (silent backward counting in steps of seven). Participants answered factual multiple-choice questions about the videos after the attentive session. Recorded signals include EEG, EOG, ECG, respiration, gaze, pupil size, and head position. This is Experiment 4 of the Brain, Body, and Behavior Dataset (BBBD). Note: the dataset README describes the design inconsistently (five versus six videos, and both sessions labelled attentive); the description here follows the README's experiment setup section (six videos, an attentive session followed by a distracted session).
datasets.authors: Jens Madsen, Nikhil Kuppa, Lucas Parra

datasets.name: Penn Electrophysiology of Encoding and Retrieval Study (PEERS)
datasets.description: The Penn Electrophysiology of Encoding and Retrieval Study (PEERS) characterizes behavioral and electrophysiological correlates of memory encoding and retrieval in highly practiced individuals. Across five PEERS experiments, more than 300 subjects contributed over 7,000 ninety-minute memory testing sessions with EEG. This dataset includes three free recall experiments: ltpFR (PEERS1-3), ltpFR2 (PEERS4), and VFFR (PEERS5).
datasets.authors: Michael J. Kahana, Joseph H. Rudoler, Lynn J. Lohnas, Karl Healey, Ada Aka, Adam Broitman, Elizabeth Crutchley, Patrick Crutchley, Kylie H. Alm, Brandon S. Katerman, Nicole E. Miller, Joel R. Kuhn, Yuxuan Li, Nicole M. Long, Jonathan Miller, Madison D. Paron, Jesse K. Pazdera, Isaac Pedisich, Christoph T. Weidemann

datasets.name: Liu et al. 2025 — Lower limb motor imagery EEG dataset based on the multi-paradigm and longitudinal-training of stroke patients (Tianjin University)
datasets.description: This dataset contains scalp EEG recordings from 27 stroke patients performing lower-limb motor imagery during rehabilitation. It uses a multi-paradigm protocol with a longitudinal, repeated-session training design. The data support research on motor-imagery brain-computer interfaces for lower-limb and gait rehabilitation after stroke.
datasets.authors: Yuan Liu, Zhuolan Gui, De Yan, Zhuang Wang, Ruisi Gao, Ningxin Han, Junying Chen, Jialing Wu, Dong Ming

datasets.name: Disentangling objects' contextual associations from perceptual and conceptual attributes using time-resolved neural decoding
datasets.description: Raw 128-channel EEG data from 20 observers viewing object images in a rapid presentation paradigm, together with representational dissimilarity matrices. The dataset supports time-resolved neural decoding analyses that separate objects' contextual associations from their perceptual and conceptual attributes. One participant was excluded because of a technical recording error, leaving 19 usable participants.
datasets.authors: Kim, Ariel*, Quek, Genevieve*, Moerel, Denise*, Gorton, Olivia, Carlson, Thomas

datasets.name: EEG and autonomic responses during emotional word association
datasets.description: This dataset contains synchronized EEG, autonomic physiological recordings, and behavioral responses collected during an emotional word association task centered on fear-related concepts. Participants either selected suggested words or generated new ones. Eight-channel EEG, electrodermal activity, blood volume pulse, interbeat interval, skin temperature, and word events with semantic similarity scores between consecutive words are included.
datasets.authors: Manuel Cebral-Loureda

datasets.name: The NIMH Healthy Research Volunteer Dataset
datasets.description: A large-scale dataset characterizing healthy research volunteers recruited at the NIMH intramural program. It combines clinical assessments, mood psychometrics, neuropsychological and cognitive testing, structural and functional MRI, diffusion imaging, and a comprehensive MEG battery. Data are shared in BIDS format to support investigations of normal cognition and mood regulation.
datasets.authors: Allison C. Nugent, Adam G Thomas, Margaret Mahoney, Alison Gibbons, Jarrod Smith, Antoinette Charles, Jacob S Shaw, Jeffrey D Stout, Anna M Namyst, Arshitha Basavaraj, Eric Earl, Dustin Moraczewski, Emily Guinee, Michael Liu, Travis Riddle, Joseph Snow, Shruti Japee, Morgan Andrews, Adriana Pavletic, Stephen Sinclair, Vinai Roopchansingh, Peter A Bandettini, Joyce Chung

datasets.name: LittlePrince_MEG_French_Listen_Pallier2025
datasets.description: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from 58 healthy native French-speaking adults who listened to the French audiobook of Le Petit Prince, split into 9 runs of about 11 minutes each. The dataset includes simultaneous EOG and ECG, plus T1-weighted anatomical MRI for source reconstruction. It supports research on naturalistic speech comprehension and decoding of individual words from non-invasive brain recordings.
datasets.authors: Corentin Bel, Julie Bonnaire, Christophe Pallier, Jean-Rémi King

datasets.name: Resting-state EEG data before and after cognitive activity across the adult lifespan and a 5-year follow-up
datasets.description: This dataset contains 64-channel resting-state EEG from 608 healthy adults aged 20-70 years, recorded for three minutes each with eyes closed and eyes open. Recordings were made before and after a 2-hour block of demanding cognitive tasks. A subsample of 208 participants also completed a follow-up session about five years after baseline. The data come from the Dortmund Vital Study on healthy cognitive aging and are provided as raw, non-preprocessed EEG in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Edmund Wascher, Daniel Schneider, Patrick D. Gajewski, Stephan Getzmann

datasets.name: LittlePrince_MEG_French_Read_Pallier2025
datasets.description: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from 50 healthy native French-speaking adults reading the French text of Le Petit Prince using a rapid serial visual presentation paradigm. The text was split into nine runs of about 8 minutes each. The dataset includes T1-weighted anatomical MRI, FreeSurfer reconstructions, and preprocessed MEG derivatives. It is intended for studying the neural basis of naturalistic reading and language comprehension.
datasets.authors: Corentin Bel, Julie Bonnaire, Jean-Rémi King, Christophe Pallier

datasets.name: P-ary m-sequence-based c-VEP dataset from Martínez-Cagigal et al. (2023)
datasets.description: EEG dataset of a code-modulated visual evoked potential (c-VEP) brain-computer interface that uses p-ary (non-binary) m-sequences. Sixteen healthy participants were recorded with 16 EEG channels at 256 Hz. Each participant completed five conditions, stored as separate sessions, with eight runs per session (six for training, two for testing). The dataset accompanies a study of more comfortable c-VEP BCIs based on non-binary m-sequences and is distributed in BIDS format via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Víctor Martínez-Cagigal, Eduardo Santamaría-Vázquez, Sergio Pérez-Velasco, Diego Marcos-Martínez, Selene Moreno-Calderón, Roberto Hornero

datasets.name: Speier et al. 2017 — A comparison of stimulus types in online classification of the P300 speller using language models
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 10 healthy participants performing an online P300 row-column speller task with a 6x6 character matrix. The study compared two stimulus types, Famous Faces and Inverting, in combination with language models for online classification. Data were recorded from 32 channels at 256 Hz across two sessions per subject with three runs each, and are annotated with HED tags.
datasets.authors: William Speier, Corey Arnold, Aniket Deshpande, Nader Pouratian

datasets.name: planmemreplay
datasets.description: MEG recordings from a study of replay during planning and memory maintenance, associated with the paper 'Distinct replay signatures for planning and memory maintenance'. The dataset includes MEG data with a trigger channel for event marking, plus event files with onsets provided for completeness. Visual event timing has an estimated projector delay of about 20 ms, measured with a photodiode.
datasets.authors: G. Elliott Wimmer, Yunzhe Liu, Daniel C. McNamee, Raymond J. Dolan

datasets.name: Shin et al. 2017 (Experiment A) — Open Access Dataset for EEG+NIRS Single-Trial Classification
datasets.description: An open access dataset for hybrid brain-computer interface research combining EEG and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS). This portion (Experiment A) contains recordings from 29 healthy participants performing left versus right hand kinesthetic motor imagery over multiple sessions. The data include 30 EEG channels plus EOG, are preprocessed, and are annotated with HED tags. They support single-trial classification and multimodal BCI validation.
datasets.authors: Jaeyoung Shin, Alexander von Lühmann, Benjamin Blankertz, Do-Won Kim, Jichai Jeong, Han-Jeong Hwang, Klaus-Robert Müller

datasets.name: ISRUC-Sleep: A comprehensive public dataset for sleep researchers.
datasets.description: ISRUC-Sleep is a public collection of overnight polysomnographic recordings with manual sleep stage annotations, organized into three subgroups that include healthy subjects, patients with sleep disorders, and multiple-night recordings. Signals include EEG, EOG, EMG and respiratory channels. Each recording was scored in 30-second epochs by two expert scorers. The dataset supports research on automatic sleep staging and sleep-disordered breathing, and has been converted to BIDS.
datasets.authors: Sirvan Khalighi, Teresa Sousa, Jose Moutinho Santos, Urbano Nunes

datasets.name: Naturalistic viewing: An open-access dataset using simultaneous EEG-fMRI
datasets.description: This dataset contains simultaneously recorded EEG and fMRI data from 22 adults aged 23 to 51 years, collected at the Nathan Kline Institute while participants watched naturalistic video stimuli. It also includes eye tracking, physiological (respiration) recordings, demographic information, and behavioral measures such as sleep and caffeine intake. The goal is to investigate the relationship between electrical brain activity and hemodynamic fluctuations.
datasets.authors: Qawi K Telesford, Eduardo Gonzalez-Moreira, Ting Xu, Yiwen Tian, Stanley Colcombe, Jessica Cloud, Brian Edward Russ, Arnaud Falchier, Maximilian Nentwich, Jens Madsen, Lucas Parra, Charles Schroeder, Michael Milham, Alexandre Rosa Franco

datasets.name: Romani et al. 2025 — BrainForm: a Serious Game for BCI Training and Data Collection (P300 ERP, University of Trento)
datasets.description: This dataset contains scalp EEG recordings from 22 participants who played BrainForm, a gamified P300 event-related potential brain-computer interface built for scalable data collection with consumer hardware and a minimal setup. Participants completed repeated runs of a P300 spelling/selection task at two task complexities. The data support study of BCI skill acquisition across sessions and of how different visual stimulation textures affect perception and performance.
datasets.authors: Michele Romani, Devis Zanoni, Elisabetta Farella, Luca Turchet

datasets.name: Wang et al. 2024 — Brain Treebank: Large-scale intracranial recordings from naturalistic language stimuli
datasets.description: The Brain Treebank is a large-scale intracranial EEG (stereo-EEG) dataset recorded at 2048 Hz from 10 epilepsy patients while they watched Hollywood movies, totalling about 43 hours across 26 movie trials and 1,688 electrodes. Movie audio was transcribed with manually annotated word onsets and parsed into Universal Dependencies syntax trees, grounding the neural recordings in naturalistic language. This version is converted to BIDS-iEEG (BrainVision) and includes electrode metadata with parcel and lobe indices.
datasets.authors: Christopher Wang, Adam Yaari, Aaditya K Singh, Vighnesh Subramaniam, Dana Rosenfarb, Jan DeWitt, Pranav Misra, Joseph R Madsen, Scellig Stone, Gabriel Kreiman, Boris Katz, Ignacio Cases, Andrei Barbu

datasets.name: Mainsah et al. 2025 — bigP3BCI: An Open, Diverse and Machine Learning Ready P300-based Brain-Computer Interface Dataset (Study P)
datasets.description: Study P of the bigP3BCI collection, an open, machine-learning-ready P300-based brain-computer interface dataset. It contains 32-channel EEG recorded at 256 Hz from 19 participants with ALS, each over two sessions, while they used a 9x8 character grid speller with predictive and non-predictive spelling paradigms. Target and non-target flash events are annotated with HED tags, and the data are reformatted from the original PhysioNet release into BIDS.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: Yang et al. 2025 — A multi-day and high-quality EEG dataset for motor imagery brain-computer interface
datasets.description: A multi-day EEG dataset for motor imagery brain-computer interface (MI-BCI) research collected at Shanghai University (WBCIC-SHU). It contains recordings from 51 healthy, BCI-naive participants who performed left- and right-hand motor imagery over three sessions on different days. A subset of 11 participants also performed a three-class paradigm that adds foot-hooking imagery. Recordings were made with a 59-channel EEG system and the dataset is accompanied by benchmark classification results using CSP, FBCSP, EEGNet, deepConvNet and FBCNet.
datasets.authors: Banghua Yang, Fenqi Rong, Yunlong Xie, Du Li, Jiayang Zhang, Fu Li, Guangming Shi, Xiaorong Gao

datasets.name: Shi et al. 2025 — HEFMI-ICH: a hybrid EEG-fNIRS motor imagery dataset for brain-computer interface in intracerebral hemorrhage
datasets.description: HEFMI-ICH is a hybrid EEG-fNIRS motor imagery dataset for brain-computer interface research in intracerebral hemorrhage. This BIDS-formatted release contains 32-channel EEG from 37 participants (17 healthy controls and 20 ICH patients), recorded across up to 3 sessions per participant. Participants performed two-class left- and right-hand motor imagery, with 15 trials per class in each session. The data support rehabilitation-oriented BCI development and classifier benchmarking.
datasets.authors: Jian Shi, Danyang Chen, Xingwei Zhao, Zhixian Zhao, Shengjie Li, Yeguang Xu, Tao Ding, Zheng Zhu, Peng Zhang, Qing Ye, Yingxin Tang, Ping Zhang, Bo Tao, Zhouping Tang

datasets.name: Castillos et al. 2023, m-sequence c-VEP, 100% amplitude depth: Burst c-VEP Based BCI: Optimizing stimulus design for enhanced classification with minimal calibration data and improved user experience
datasets.description: EEG dataset of a 4-class code-modulated visual evoked potential (c-VEP) reactive brain-computer interface study with 12 healthy participants. This subset contains the m-sequence c-VEP condition at 100% amplitude depth, recorded with a 32-channel BrainProducts LiveAmp system at 500 Hz. The study compared burst and m-sequence codes at two amplitude depths, assessing classification accuracy with minimal calibration data and user experience.
datasets.authors: Kalou Cabrera Castillos, Simon Ladouce, Ludovic Darmet, Frédéric Dehais

datasets.name: Castillos et al. 2023, Burst c-VEP, 40% amplitude depth: Burst c-VEP Based BCI: Optimizing stimulus design for enhanced classification with minimal calibration data and improved user experience
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 12 healthy participants performing an offline 4-class reactive BCI task based on code-modulated visual evoked potentials (c-VEP). The dataset covers the 'Burst c-VEP' condition at 40% amplitude depth, in which short bursts of aperiodic flashes are presented at 2-4 flashes per second. It supports work on stimulus design, visual comfort, and CNN-based bitwise decoding with minimal calibration data.
datasets.authors: Kalou Cabrera Castillos, Simon Ladouce, Ludovic Darmet, Frédéric Dehais

datasets.name: Castillos et al. 2023, Burst c-VEP, 100% amplitude depth: Burst c-VEP Based BCI: Optimizing stimulus design for enhanced classification with minimal calibration data and improved user experience
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 12 healthy participants performing an offline 4-class code-modulated visual evoked potential (c-VEP) task with burst stimulation sequences at 100% amplitude depth. The dataset accompanies a study comparing burst c-VEP codes with m-sequences to improve classification accuracy, reduce calibration data and improve user experience in reactive brain-computer interfaces. Data were acquired with a 32-channel BrainProducts LiveAmp system at 500 Hz.
datasets.authors: Kalou Cabrera Castillos, Simon Ladouce, Ludovic Darmet, Frédéric Dehais

datasets.name: Hinss et al. 2021 — Open multi-session and multi-task EEG cognitive Dataset for passive brain-computer Interface Applications
datasets.description: This dataset contains 62-channel EEG recordings from 15 healthy participants across two sessions each, collected for passive brain-computer interface research in neuroergonomics. It includes resting-state periods and three difficulty levels (easy, medium, difficult) of the MATB-II multitasking environment, supporting cross-session and cross-subject mental workload estimation. This BIDS version was regenerated through MOABB with corrected sampling-rate handling (250 Hz epochs).
datasets.authors: Marcel F. Hinss, Emilie S. Jahanpour, Bertille Somon, Lou Pluchon, Frédéric Dehais, Raphaëlle N. Roy

datasets.name: Castillos et al. 2023, m-sequence c-VEP, 40% amplitude depth: Burst c-VEP Based BCI: Optimizing stimulus design for enhanced classification with minimal calibration data and improved user experience
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 12 healthy participants performing an offline 4-class code-modulated visual evoked potential (c-VEP) reactive BCI task. This subset contains the m-sequence condition at 40% amplitude depth, from a factorial study that compared burst and m-sequence codes at 100% and 40% modulation depth. The dataset supports evaluation of CNN-based decoding with minimal calibration data and of the visual comfort of reduced-intensity stimuli.
datasets.authors: Kalou Cabrera Castillos, Simon Ladouce, Ludovic Darmet, Frédéric Dehais
